RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-DDD103990C-51911
Member: Sawyer Hayes (ID W641457203)
Plan: Superior HealthPlan (Ambetter), Texas Marketplace
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-14
Requested service: Shoulder labral/instability repair, CPT 29806
Treating surgeon: Dr. Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806 (arthroscopic shoulder labral/instability repair) described in the above-referenced notice. The stated reason for denial is that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I am requesting a full reconsideration of this determination based on the clinical record summarized below.

**1. The record documents a completed, supervised course of conservative treatment.**

My clinical file includes:
- A physical therapy discharge note documenting a 10-week supervised course of physical therapy (2026-05-05 to 2026-07-14, 16 completed visits) focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening, with concurrent activity modification;
- Six months of NSAID use during symptomatic flares;
- No corticosteroid injection, because injection is not clinically indicated for glenohumeral instability.

I understand that the plan's clinical review for shoulder surgery is performed by its delegated vendor, Evolent (per Superior/Ambetter's own Pre-Auth Tool, which identifies Evolent as the entity that verifies "musculoskeletal services for shoulder... surgery"). I was able to locate and review portions of Evolent's Shoulder Arthroscopy clinical guideline. That guideline states, under "General Requirements for Elective Surgery of the Shoulder," that non-operative management "when required... may include one or more of the following: Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program; Rest or activity modification; Application of heat or ice; Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated); Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial, intra-articular space, or bicipital groove." My records document supervised physical therapy, activity modification, and more than four weeks of oral NSAIDs — satisfying multiple of the listed modalities named in the guideline itself.

I want to be transparent that I was not able to obtain or verify the exact text of the specific indication section of this guideline that addresses labral repair for anterior instability (Bankart lesion) — the section that would presumably set out the precise duration or components of conservative care required for CPT 29806 specifically. I am not able to quote that section because I have not been given it, and I am not attempting to reconstruct or guess its wording. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Superior HealthPlan/Evolent provide me and my surgeon with the complete, specific medical-necessity criteria that were actually applied to this request — including the section addressing anterior-inferior labral tear/Bankart lesion repair — so that we may respond to it directly. Under applicable claims-procedure requirements, I understand I am entitled to receive the specific rule, guideline, or criterion relied upon in this denial, free of charge, upon request.

**2. The clinical picture supports surgery regardless of further non-operative trial.**

Independent of the conservative-care documentation above, the clinical findings in my file support surgical repair:
- Twelve months of recurrent instability with apprehension;
- Three documented anterior dislocations since symptom onset, the most recent requiring emergency department reduction;
- MR arthrogram (2026-07-01) confirming an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion and glenoid bone loss under 10%, with an intact rotator cuff;
- Positive apprehension and relocation tests on exam, with increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing, and full strength;
- Functional loss: inability to perform overhead reaching and inability to return to lifting duties at work;
- No active infection, no untreated substance dependency, BMI 29, non-smoker — i.e., no contraindications to surgery.

Recurrent traumatic anterior dislocation with an imaging-confirmed Bankart lesion is a well-recognized indication for surgical stabilization, particularly after a course of supervised rehabilitation has already been completed, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

**3. Requested action**

I ask that Superior HealthPlan/Evolent:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29806 for Sawyer Hayes; or, in the alternative,
2. Provide the complete text of the specific medical-necessity criteria (including the section addressing anterior-inferior labral tear/Bankart lesion repair) that were applied to this request, so that my surgeon and I may respond to the specific criteria relied upon; and
3. Confirm that this appeal has been received and is being processed within the timeframe Superior/Ambetter has published for standard member appeals (decision within 30 days, or within 1 working day if expedited review is warranted).

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-calendar-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-10). Enclosed with this letter are: the physical therapy discharge summary, the 2026-07-01 MR arthrogram report, office visit notes documenting exam findings and dislocation history, and a letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist. Please contact me at [member phone number] or [member email address], or my surgeon's office at [surgeon office phone/fax], with any questions or if additional records are needed.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Hayes
